title: About the Week
lede: One co-hosted programme over four days, bridging the commitments of COP31 and investment-ready projects.
background: Energy Planning Week 2026 convenes in Bonn two weeks after COP31 closes. Co-hosted by IRENA and GET.transform, it is the first chance for the energy planning community to work out how COP31 commitments become the scenarios, roadmaps and project pipelines needed to deliver them.

The constraint is less the availability of capital than the capacity to direct it: investment follows credible national plans, institutions that sustain them across political cycles, and regional frameworks for shared infrastructure. Planning itself is also changing. Storage, distributed generation and flexibility are reshaping what models must represent, supply-chain and price shocks have undercut pre-2022 assumptions, and climate risk and new methods such as artificial intelligence need to be built in.

The Week brings together three efforts: the Long-term Energy Scenarios (LTES) Network, where government planners strengthen scenario practice; the Global Coalition for Energy Planning (GCEP), which links plans to investment; and GET.transform, a technical assistance programme implemented by GIZ and co-funded by the European Union, Germany, Norway, the Netherlands, Sweden and Austria.
objectives: Connect scenario governance, investment signals and implementation, so COP31 commitments become investment-ready projects.
Build the mandates, skills, data and modelling capacity that keep planning on track across political cycles.
Tackle the planning-to-investment bottlenecks raised in LTES and GCEP regional dialogues — grids, flexibility, project preparation and finance-facing signals.
Foster peer exchange among planners, financiers, regulators, utilities and partner institutions.
audience: Government energy planners and policymakers, alongside industry, finance, regulators, utilities, intergovernmental organisations and the modelling community.
